origin: bounded current-frontier maintenance from three immutable independent source reviews

items.title: Stock Lua numeric ABI successor accepted at source
items.statement: Independent review accepts HighBar c1471bb2fae0c680f0bdecb62ad3d051b8ef422e (tree 2df62bb057d291899688c9ca150e5cdd818a4e4a) for the exact stock2639 observer source route. Actual stock Lua5.1 with float-number semantics and 14 focused tests pass; the deterministic 5019-byte overlay has SHA-256 c7d6b583a954e7c2b0fdbb9c697355aaf1d2a1cd24049c3d30b9e01dfdd99d4c. This closes the three source/numeric blockers in prior 2a7 while leaving discovery, transport, runtime identity, signed-zero transport, and native acceptance unproved.

scope.applicability: source and numeric-ABI acceptance only; prior 2a7 failed attempt remains historical

evidence.summary: Exact source identity, three blocker closures, independent stock Lua float-number harness, 14 tests, package identity, and retained runtime gates.
evidence.scope: Exact independently reviewed source candidate and stated checks only; no installed runtime or native acceptance.

items.title: Stock float32 and SHA byte codec repair is source accepted
items.statement: The accepted c147 Lua successor implements SHA-256 with bounded byte limbs and obtains float32 bytes through stock synced VFS.PackF32 with endian and signed-zero checks. Independent actual stock Lua5.1 float-number tests cover low mantissa bits, subnormal extremes, finite maximum, negative zero, actor0, and frozen bridge vectors. Actual engine command transport remains a native gate.

scope.applicability: accepted source/numeric boundary, with actual engine parameter transport still unproved

evidence.summary: Independent review verifies the bounded limb SHA and PackF32 repair under actual stock Lua float-number semantics.

items.title: FSBar stock consumer candidate is source blocked
items.statement: Independent review blocks FSBar 611f4d118692fdf93d046fb7d82b4bf77318b0ec: production LiveBoundary drops EvidenceScheme 2 to default 0, a fresh F# test build fails on native/browser enum collisions hidden by stale --no-build output, and the exported oracle accepts NaN, oversized integers, missing rows, and unrelated actor evidence while reporting observed claims. No consumer source acceptance or native acceptance exists.

scope.applicability: source blocked; repair owner active; no product or runtime acceptance

items.title: Cross-codec fixtures must exercise the production projection
items.statement: A manually authored browser queue with EvidenceScheme 2 can pass while the real native-to-browser LiveBoundary projection silently emits default 0. Qualification for cross-codec fields requires a production ingress-to-projection-to-wire round trip, including legacy/default and unavailable forms; a direct fixture does not prove the deployed conversion.

scope.applicability: general verification lesson grounded in the exact blocked stock candidate

evidence.summary: Production probe observes native scheme2 becoming browser scheme0 while manually authored fixtures pass.

items.title: No-build test success does not qualify changed generated source
items.statement: A 17-test --no-build result used an older assembly that lacked the newly generated EvidenceScheme field; rebuilding the changed source exposes enum type errors. After generated contracts or production projections change, qualification must rebuild the affected source before tests, and must distinguish discovery, compilation, and execution.

scope.applicability: cross-project process lesson; does not make a source or runtime claim beyond the reviewed candidate

evidence.summary: Fresh F# build fails where the earlier no-build suite used stale assemblies.

items.title: Stock native reader compiles but production plugin source is blocked
items.statement: The stock reader candidate still compiles against Recoil2639 and its parser/state tests pass, but independent review of HighBar 564f84e7beec91cc602a3ecca67a60ea9c23e917 (tree 48f4f054c4fed4eb3af89a442dbab7814e6e2f1d) blocks source admission: the guarded dispatch re-enters a nonrecursive authority mutex, decisive deadline and actor checks occur before a potentially slow CallRules reread, the compatibility predicate rejects the selected headless tuple while admitting a broad 2025 family, and INT32_MIN command projection performs undefined signed negation. Plugin SHA 8891762ffe6976195a11d3319c8f1b7f8ebacb952215982ddf1a0bbef8951675 remains source/build evidence only.

scope.applicability: source blocked pending coherent repair and rereview; no runtime acceptance

items.title: What still blocks stock native acceptance after Lua source acceptance?
items.statement: The stock-compatible Lua numeric source gate is closed at c147, but coherent delivery remains blocked by the reviewed FSBar production projection/build/oracle defects and HighBar authority-lock/deadline/version/INT32_MIN defects. After source repairs and rereviews, open gates still include a joined protected source set, exact overlay/plugin discovery, selected and loaded stock executable identity, real CallRules and signed-zero transport, catalogue/content/profile/actor-lifetime binding, final reread and equality, and all required native journeys.
